# CSV export button — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for the CSV export button when the rows on screen need to leave as a file. The CSV is built from data, never from the rendered grid — `columns` are key and title pairs and `rows` are plain records — so what downloads is what the host passed, not what the grid painted. `filename` and `label` name the file and the button, and values serialise as-is: there is no cell formatting, so shape the rows before passing them. `onExport` receives the CSV text instead of downloading it, which is the seam for tests, share sheets and analytics. The button owns its own rendering — no variant, size, icon, children or click passthrough to collide with — so the export is one declaration.

## Native

### Features

Reach for the CSV export button when the rows on screen need to leave as text for the share sheet. The CSV is built from data, never from the rendered grid — `columns` are key and title pairs and `rows` are plain records — so what exports is what the host passed, not what the grid painted. On native there is no silent file save, so `onExport` is required: every export goes through it to the share sheet, the file write or the test, observing the same text a download would carry. `filename` and `label` name the file and the button, and values serialise as-is: there is no cell formatting, so shape the rows before passing them.
